newsitem.title: USA: CDW Computer says Q4 demand remains strong.
newsitem.headline: CDW Computer says Q4 demand remains strong.

text.p: CDW Computer Centers Inc, a direct marketer of microcomputer products, said Wednesday its sales outlook for the fourth quarter is favorable as customer demand has remained strong through the first 15 days of October.

Earlier today, CDW reported 1996 its third quarter sales rose 49 percent from the year ago quarter to $240.3 million. Net income increased 83 percent from last year to $9.7 million while per share earnings were up 76 percent to $0.44.
"We continue to experience strong demand as our customer base transitions to new technologies and faster processing speeds," CDW chairman Michael Krasny said in a statement.
CDW said a recent authorization to direct market Compaq Presario and Hewlett- Packard Vectra 500 lines should add to its desktop product offerings in the fourth quarter.
Gains continue to be fueled by sales of high-end notebook and laptop computers, as well as multi-media products, input devices and data storage products, CDW said.
This demand is driven, in part, by customers adopting new 32 bit software architecture which requires faster processors, more memory and additional storage capacity, CDW said.
The number of customers serviced by CDW rose 27 percent to 444,000 for the twelve months ended September 30, 1996.
Third quarter 1995 introduction of Windows 95 did not have a significant impact on third quarter comparisons, CDW noted.
CDW's third quarter gross profit margin was 13.1 percent of net sales, up from 12.7 percent in the 1995 third quarter but down from the 13.5 percent in the 1996 second quarter.
Gross profit margins depend on product mix, market conditions, vendor support programs, the value of the dollar and other factors which may vary, the company said.
Total catalog circulation in the third quarter grew 66 percent over a year ago to over 12 million but declined slightly from the second quarter of 1996.
Working capital as of September 30, 1996 was about $116 million with about $66 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.
A new warehouse, distribution, telemarketing and corporate office facility should be ready for occupancy in the third quarter of 1997, CDW said.
